|\|   \|   \|<br>\|---\|---\|<br>\|**🛈**\|**Joe Kendra call at 9:52a on 6/21/24**<br><br>  <br>- At a Pearl datacenter in Atlanta (not a STACK dc), a whip feeding a RPP at the rack level experienced an arc flash when being manipulated/handled by a person (not sure company or discipline).<br>- After inspection of the whip in question, metal shavings were found.<br>- After further inspection of additional whips at the dc where the incident took place, it was found to be a systemic issue across the site.<br>- The same contract crew that installed the whips at the Pearl datacenter in Atlanta performed the same work at NVA02D/E.<br>- Pearl is ordering the inspection of all whips at NVA02D/E for similar metal shavings to prevent a reoccurrence.<br>    - Ian S. is writing up a more comprehensive overview to send out to a wider audience.<br>    - Daniel Stevenson (ACOM) is working with local Pearl representatives at NVA02D/E to create a MOP(s) to address this ask by Pearl.<br>    - Confirmed with Kendra, Daniel Stevenson, & Reid Thomas (ACOM) that each whip is able to be isolated (de-energized) for inspection while still feeding the racks through a redundant feed.<br>    - Confirmed with Kendra, Daniel S., & Reid T. that this scope of work would not require Energized Electrical Work Permits (EEWP), as no one will be exposed to energized electrical conductors.\||
